Subject: DPA routing pocket guide for EMEA marketplace procurement

Marissa / Ben —

Quick ask from BrightMarket procurement (cc'd): they need a short, scannable deliverable we can hand to marketplace sellers during onboarding. High-level asks: a one-page "pocket guide" that summarizes routing choices (SCCs vs UK IDTA/addendum vs TIA/DTIA), a short checklist of required evidence for subprocessors (what level of artifact we accept: SOC2, attestations, KMS configuration screenshots, residency claims), and an Excel cert matrix that maps proof -> acceptance criteria.

Constraints / context: EMEA procurement wants something by next week (target 2026-09-15) to include with their onboarding packet. This is aimed at non-legal procurement folks at partners — crisp language, a few callouts about when an exception is needed (e.g., onshore-only hosting requests), and links to canonical Redwood artifacts.

I started a skeleton and attached it (skeleton-dpa-pocket-guide.docx) — can you two take primary ownership? Proposed split: Marissa — legal summary + checklist + wording for UK Addendum; Ben — cert matrix and operational acceptance thresholds + example evidence. I'll consolidate and publish the two-pager (one-pager + matrix) and route to BrightMarket for signoff.

Julia — feel free to add any specific fields your procurement team wants in the matrix (billing contact, contract clause acceptance, sandbox residency notes) — happy to slot them in.

Next steps: can you reply with ownership/ETA?

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — happy to own the legal wording. A couple quick clarifications so I don't over/under-spec: 

- Do you want the pocket guide to recommend a default routing (e.g., SCCs + EU-hosting preferred) or remain neutral and list tradeoffs? My vote is a short recommendation + two bullets of when to escalate to legal (onshore-only, regulated data categories, or custom subprocessor requests).

- For subprocessors: do we want to list precise evidence examples? I suggest we include 3 tiers: (1) minimal (self-attestation + subprocessor list), (2) standard (SOC 2 Type II or ISO/IEC 27001 + data processing addendum), (3) elevated (KMS/HSM proof, in-country residency attestation, on-site audits). Provide a one-line example for each.

- UK Addendum: should we include a single-line note linking to the UK IDTA and point buyers to the signing flow, or add the actual checkbox text vendors must accept? I think linking + callout is enough for a pocket guide.

I started a Google doc and added a short draft section for the three-tier evidence approach: https://drive.google.com/example/dpa-pocket-guide-draft — I'll refine and put version comments.

ETA: I can get a legal-first draft (one pager prose + checklist) by EOD Thu 2026-09-10.

—Marissa
